summary: Comprehensive backend + frontend testing of Automated Loan Eligibility Engine (Phase 1-3). Backend: 8/8 pytest cases PASS (Policy CRUD, active-only filter, admin-only RBAC, eligibility engine against 27 policies, invalid lead 404, history retrieval, unauthenticated blocking). Frontend: 27 policy cards render on /bank-policy-master with Add button; /eligibility-check/{leadId} renders Profile Summary (CIBIL/NetSalary/EMI/FOIR/Requested/Company), Comparison table with 8 rows, Missing Data warning, POSSIBLY ELIGIBLE section with 27 cards, expandable BankCard with policy grid, BT/Top-up details, PASS/FAIL/WARNING rule tables, Print window opens with 28k chars formatted report, History panel loads previous snapshots. All data-testid selectors resolved.
passed_tests: POST /api/bank-policies/check-eligibility/{lead_id} evaluates all 27 policies, returns sorted results, enriched fields (bt_info, reasons_pass/fail/warning), correct counts
BankPolicyMaster UI: 27 cards + Add Lender Policy button visible
EligibilityCheck UI: Profile Summary, Comparison table (8 rows), Recheck/Print/History buttons render
Missing Data warning shown for Present Employment, Company Category, Total Employment
Bank card expands to show policy grid, BT & Top-up section, Eligibility Criteria Met table, Risks / Missing Data table
Print button opens new window with formatted HTML report (~28k chars, includes h1, comparison table, per-bank details)
History panel loads previous eligibility snapshots (9 rows for test lead)
NOT ELIGIBLE toggle present (test lead has 0 not-eligible; all 27 are possibly_eligible due to missing FOIR/company_type)
critical_code_review_comments: backend/bank_policies.py:11 - DB_NAME uses default 'test_database' when env missing. Since backend/.env has no DB_NAME and rest of app uses same fallback (verified), this is consistent, but recommend adding DB_NAME to backend/.env explicitly for clarity.
bank_policies.py:164 evaluate_lead_against_policy is 230+ lines; consider splitting rule checks into named functions for maintainability.
bank_policies.py:476 stores snapshot then does snapshot.pop('_id', None) - since motor mutates the dict adding _id, this is correct, but cleaner to use a separate insert dict.
EligibilityCheck.js is 590 lines and exceeds the 700-line guideline for a single file only slightly - future BankCard extraction to its own file recommended.
handlePrint uses document.write which is deprecated; consider building via DOM APIs or a hidden iframe.
seed_data_creation: None new. Used existing test lead f3a38ad7-eb68-4145-897b-0a17e022a81d (Raju Bhai). Created and deleted TEST_BANK_XYZ policy in CRUD test.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Auth login returns 'token' (not 'access_token'). Use helper that tries both. 27 bank policies are seeded. Test lead f3a38ad7... has salary=100000, cibil=750 but missing FOIR/company_type/employment months so all 27 policies come back as 'possibly_eligible' (0 eligible, 0 not_eligible). To test NOT ELIGIBLE cards you would need a lead with low salary/CIBIL to trigger fails. Backend router mounted at /api/bank-policies with endpoints /policies (CRUD), /check-eligibility/{lead_id}, /eligibility-history/{lead_id}.
